chunks: Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā narrated from Muḥammad ibn Ādam, from his father, from Abū al-Ḥasan al-Riḍā, from his forefathers, from ʿAlī عليه السلام, who said: The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله said to ʿAlī عليه السلام:

O ʿAlī, do not consult a coward, for he will constrain for you the way out. And do not consult a miser, for he will hold you back from your goal. And do not consult a greedy person, for he will make covetousness seem fair to you. And know that cowardice, miserliness, and greed are an inborn disposition brought together by سوء الظنّ.

key_terms.الْمَخْرَجَ: the way out or avenue of resolution
key_terms.بَخِيلًا: a miserly person who withholds and discourages noble aims
key_terms.جَبَانًا: a cowardly person whose fear constricts decisions
key_terms.حَرِيصًا: a greedy person driven by excessive craving
key_terms.سُوءُ الظَّنِّ: bad opinion; here, a corrupt underlying assumption that feeds these vices

ai.seo_question: Whom should a believer avoid consulting according to the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله?
ai.summary: The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله warns Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام against taking counsel from people whose inner vices distort judgment. Cowardice, miserliness, and greed are presented as rooted in سوء الظنّ, making this hadith a concise teaching on character, consultation, and moral discernment.
